text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
CORN SALE - Taiwan's FGEP corn-buying group on Tuesday bought a shipment of 54,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn from Agrex, traders said. Delivery was set for December at 89 cents over December.

CORN AND BARLEY SALE - The Cyprus Grain Commission has accepted a tender from Toepfer Athens for 25,000 tonnes of barley at $148.62 per tonne and one from Andre and Cie for 18,000 tonnes of corn at $158.95, it said. Prices are C&F and both shipments are scheduled for the second half of October.

WHEAT SALE - The CCC bought 42,778 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat under the export donation program to Georgia. The wheat was acquired from ADM at $179.70 a tonne, FOB, Galveston, Texas. The total value of the sale was $7,687,206.

SOYBEAN MEAL SALE - The Ukraine bought about 32,780 tonnes U.S. soybean meal in bulk for December 1-15 shipment, under the PL 480, Title I export donation program, USDA said. The meal was acquired at $281.90 a tonne, FOB, Mississippi River, from Continental Grain.

RICE SALE - Jordan bought 22,500 tonnes of medium grain rice in two separate purchases comprising 15,000 tonnes of U.S. rice at $483 per tonne and 7,500 tonnes of Egyptian rice at $448 per tonne. The 15,000 tonnes of U.S. medium grain was purchased from Amman Resources who bought the cargo from a floating vessel for processing in the firm's Aqaba packaging plant. The cargo is expected in the first week of October on FOT terms. The purchase of 7,500 tonnes of Egyptian rice, supplied by Swiss Andre, was for first half November.

SOYBEAN TENDER - The Kaohsiung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association will tender on Wednesday for three 54,000-tonne shipments of U.S. soybeans, traders said. One 54,000 tonne shipment was set for December 26-January 9, U.S. Gulf and/or Jan 10-24, PNW. A second 54,000 tonne shipment was slated for Jan 17-31, U.S. Gulf and/or Feb 1-15, PNW, and a third 54,000 tonne shipment was for Feb 9-23, U.S. Gulf and/or Feb 24-March 10 PNW.

WHEAT TENDER - Surinam will seek to purchase 2,800 tonnes U.S. No.2 or better northern spring/dark northern spring wheat in bulk under the PL 480 Title I. Shipment is set for October 10-25. Bids must be submitted by September 26.

WHEAT TENDERS - Pakistan will tender for 200,000 tonnes U.S. grade 2 or better soft white wheat under the GSM-102 program for October 10-31 shipment, its U.S. export agent said. Bids are due September 29 and must remain valid until Sepember 30.

- Angola seeks 17,850 tonnes of U.S. No.2 or better PL-480 hard red winter wheat in bulk under the PL 480, Title I, export donation program, its U.S. export agent said. The delivery period is set for October 10-25. Bids must be received by September 24 and remain valid until September 25.

WHEAT TENDERS (cont.) - The CCC seeks up to 35,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 or better hard red winter or soft red winter or soft white wheat for donation to Eritrea. Shipment is set for Oct 10-Nov 5. Offers are due by Sept 26.

- Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade offered 100,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale for November shipment. October 1 is the final date for offers. Confirmation is set on October 2.
CORN TENDERS - Jordan is to seek 50,000 tonnes of U.S. Number 3 yellow corn for shipment in first half of November. Offers must be received by September 25.

- The South African Maize Board was offering up to 33,000 tonnes of white corn for export in one unit of 20,000, 25,000 or 33,000 tonnes for shipment on October 23 to November 1, from Durban. The tender closes on September 25.
- CCC said it is seeking up to 16,000 tonnes U.S. No.2 or better yellow corn for donation to Rwanda. Shipment period is set for December 5-30 and offers are due by September 24.
RICE TENDERS - Moldova will tender Wednesday for 14,000 tonnes of PL-480 long-grain milled rice for November.
MARKET TALK - French barley firmed on Tuesday following news Saudi Arabia bought about 1.4 million tonnes of barley for import from October to December, dealers said.

The purchase, which has yet to be officially confirmed, was made at prices ranging from $146 to $158 per tonne, cost and freight. Barley into Rouen for October-December delivery was quoted at 880 francs per tonne, up 10 francs on Monday. Barley into Dunkirk for the same delivery periods fetched 885 francs, also up 10 francs on the previous day. The EU, which enjoys a supply and freight advantage over other suppliers, is widely expected to help cover a large share of the contract.
